title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies
abstract: This conceptual narrative review examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in Korean language learning. The paper synthesizes recent scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean language education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics to develop an analytical framework for responsible classroom use. The review focuses on four dimensions: Korean language skills, Korean-specific linguistic and cultural features, instructional design, and governance risks. The analysis suggests that generative AI can support listening, speaking, reading, and writing when tasks are explicitly designed around Korean phonology, morphology, pragmatics, and learner purposes such as TOPIK preparation, study abroad, employment, and popular-culture engagement. It also identifies challenges in cultural-pragmatic accuracy, hallucinated expressions, assessment validity, data privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency. The paper concludes that generative AI should function as a mediated learning resource rather than a substitute for teachers, learner judgment, or culturally grounded interaction.

title: SoK: The Security-Safety Continuum of Multimodal Foundation Models
abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) integrate diverse data modalities to support complex and wide-ranging tasks. However, this integration also introduces distinct safety and security challenges. In this paper, we unify the concepts of safety and security in the context of MFMs by identifying critical threats that arise from both model behavior and system-level interactions. We propose a taxonomy grounded in information theory, evaluating risks through the concepts of channel capacity, signal, noise, and bandwidth. This perspective provides a principled way to analyze how information flows through MFMs and how vulnerabilities can emerge across modalities. Building on this foundation, we introduce a deterministic minimax formulation to analyze defense mechanisms and to study a structural asymmetry of defense in multimodal systems. Our analysis indicates that model-centric defenses, which primarily operate by suppressing noise or enhancing signal, tend to exhibit diminishing effectiveness against increasingly adaptive attacks. In contrast, system-level safeguards that constrain authorized information flow and agent behavior impose stronger limits on adversarial impact by reducing effective bandwidth. To operationalize this insight, our framework maps attacks and defenses onto information-theoretic axes, effectively organizing and reducing the defense search space. Using a proposed Defense Coverage Index (DCI) to evaluate 15 representative defenses, we observe that system-level bandwidth constraints provide stronger and more consistent protection across attack classes than brittle model-level mechanisms. Finally, we formalize an MFM ``self-destruction threshold'' that specifies when termination should be triggered, offering a concrete activation rule for circuit-breaker safeguards in multimodal systems.

title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
abstract: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic AI and optimized prompts, may be apt for tackling some of the challenges.

title: How to Build Digital Humans? From Priors to Photorealistic Avatars
abstract: Abstract This state‐of‐the‐art report provides an overview of controllable 3D human avatar creation. We describe current 3D avatar systems, which typically consist of three stages: (i) learning priors of human appearance and motion, (ii) creating a personalized avatar, and (iii) animating the avatar. To limit the scope, we focus on the prior learning and avatar creation stages. We define current avatar representations and introduce a taxonomy that categorizes existing work along multiple axes, including body regions and employed priors. We review methods for full‐body and head avatars, as well as layered representations that decompose the body into components such as hands, hair, and garments. Finally, we outline common underlying principles, reference key literature for newcomers, and discuss open challenges and future research directions.

title: Automated Question Answering for Thai Visa Services using GPT-4: System Architecture, Custom Dataset, and Performance Evaluation
venue: Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology
abstract: Thailand’s immigration system includes various visa types, such as Tourist (TR), Business (Non-Immigrant B), Education (Non-Immigrant ED), ED Plus, Media (Non-Immigrant M), Official (Non-Immigrant F), Dependent/Spouse (Non-Immigrant O), SMART, Transit, Long-Term Resident (LTR), Retirement (O-A), and Long-Stay Retirement (O-X), each governed by distinct and frequently updated policies. This complexity causes confusion and difficulties for foreign nationals in understanding required documents, eligibility criteria, and policy changes, as shown by a survey involving 75 respondents in Bangkok. Without scalable and accurate solutions, these challenges can reduce service efficiency and public trust. To address this, the study employs GPT-4, a Large Language Model (LLM), optimized with prompt engineering and few-shot learning to automatically answer visa-related questions with accurate, clear, and policy-compliant responses. A simulated dataset of 1,600 question-answer pairs was created from official Thai immigration policies. GPT-4’s performance was systematically evaluated using automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR) and human assessments of accuracy, clarity, and user satisfaction, providing a robust methodological basis for evaluating its effectiveness in public service. Results show strong performance across most categories, with the highest BLEU scores observed in Tourist (0.82), Business (0.81), and Long-Term Resident (LTR) (0.78) visa-related queries. Corresponding peak ROUGE-L scores were 0.86 for Tourist, 0.84 for Business, and 0.81 for Long-Term Resident (LTR) visas, while METEOR scores peaked at 0.79 (Tourist), 0.78 (Business), and 0.76 (Long-Term Resident (LTR)). The system achieved an overall BLEU score of 0.75, ROUGE-L of 0.79, and METEOR of 0.73. Human evaluators rated GPT-4's responses with an average score of 4.5 for accuracy, 4.6 for language clarity, and 4.4 for user satisfaction (on a 5-point scale). A Pearson correlation of 0.78 between BLEU and human-rated accuracy indicates high alignment between automated and human evaluation. These results highlight GPT-4's potential in enhancing public-facing services such as immigration services by providing accurate, clear, and policy-aligned responses. Future work will focus on multilingual support, real-time policy updates, and deployment in live service environments.

title: Online Game-based Learning via LINE Application to Enhance Parts of Speech Skills of High School Students with Hearing Impairment in the 21st Century
venue: Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology
abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an online game-based learning tool via LINE application to enhance English parts of speech skills among high school students with hearing impairments. The research objectives were to: (1) develop the online educational game, (2) assess its efficiency, (3) compare students' pre- and post-learning achievement, (4) examine students' learning progress, and (5) investigate the relationship between post-learning achievement and student satisfaction. The sample consisted of 27 high school students with hearing impairments from Surin School for the Deaf during the first semester of the 2024 academic year, selected through purposive sampling. Research instruments included the developed online game, pre- and post-tests, and a satisfaction survey. Data were analyzed using a dependent t-test, Pearson's correlation, percentages, and mean scores. The development process yielded 8 learning units and 109 online games. The system demonstrated high functionality, with an efficiency ratio of 1.46, exceeding McGuigan's criterion of 1.00. A significant improvement in students' post-test scores compared to pre-test scores was observed (p < 0.05). The average learning gain was 15.59%, which was lower than the hypothesized 50%. A significant positive correlation was found between student satisfaction and post-learning achievement (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that the developed online game-based learning tool effectively enhances English language skills among students with hearing impairments, offering insights into innovative educational approaches for this population.

title: Reframing L2 Pragmatic Competence in the Generative AI Era: A Co-Design-Oriented Critical Curriculum
abstract: The rapid incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into second-language (L2) education has reopened a foundational question in language pedagogy: what should count as successful communication when English is routinely used among speakers who do not share a native-speaker norm? Much L2 pragmatic instruction continues to treat pragmatics as the acquisition of socially appropriate forms modelled on idealised native-speaker practices. This conceptual review article proposes a co-design-oriented critical pragmatic curriculum that positions GAI (implemented primarily through large language models, or LLMs) not as an infallible tutor but as a contestable intercultural interlocutor. Drawing on English as a Lingua Franca (ELF), World Englishes, translanguaging, critical pragmatics, critical digital literacy, and design-based research (DBR), the paper advances a unified pedagogical architecture comprising three modules: Persona Engineering and Dialectic Diversity, Real-Time Meaning Negotiation, and Deconstructing Algorithmic Bias, each enacted through a four-stage learning episode (persona engineering → GAI interaction → critical negotiation → reflection and transfer) and organised within an iterative co-design cycle. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded model for integrating GAI with intercultural and critical language pedagogy while retaining teacher mediation, learner agency, multilingual resources, and ethical safeguards. It argues that the educational value of GAI lies less in making learners sound more native-like than in helping them become more observant, adaptive, critical, and strategically competent participants in multilingual communication.

title: “A Friendly Province to Come and Learn in”: Framing Healthcare Deservingness for International Students in Manitoba
abstract: Abstract In 2018, international students in Manitoba were stunned to learn that once again they no longer had access to public healthcare. Through the lens of noncitizenship assemblage, this shift is reflective of the conditional access to entitlements experienced by precarious status migrants and the frames of deservingness structuring their presence in host countries. Critical Frame Analysis was used to examine Manitoba Hansard and media from 2007–2023 to understand how healthcare for international students in Manitoba was framed. Findings indicate three frames: one in which healthcare is framed as a human right, and the others in which healthcare is positioned as a market incentive or a gesture of inclusion, both meant to attract and retain students. Although we find there is advantage to adopting a frame that connects healthcare to economic contribution for actors seeking to expand access, it nevertheless ties access to government priorities, maintaining conditionality rather than securing rights.

title: Constructing AI safety: a comparative cognitive-discursive analysis of corporate and regulatory discourses
abstract: Background The global proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has transformed safety governance into a highly contested sociopolitical battleground, yet existing discourse studies frequently under-theorize the micro-cognitive mechanisms of epistemic reality construction within AI safety standardization. Objective To investigate how corporate and regulatory actors engineer divergent cognitive realities of AI safety through specific micro-grammatical choices. Methods We proposed an integrated Cognitive-Critical Discourse Analysis framework by synthesizing Langacker's cognitive conception of reality with Fairclough's three-dimensional model, and applied it to a comparative corpus of corporate safety frameworks and regulatory policy documents. Results Tech enterprises engineer a reality of techno-pragmatic containment via active voice, high-certainty evidentiality, and immediate projection to naturalize self-regulation. Conversely, regulatory bodies construct a reality of socio-structural vulnerability using distal modals, passive constructions, and deontic mandates to legitimize state-enforced compliance. Conclusions Linguistic normalization is actively deployed to facilitate or contest corporate epistemic hegemony in AI governance. These findings provide empirical references for revising regulatory discourse and enhancing public media literacy against algorithmic exceptionalism.

title: Language outcomes in preschool children with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia
abstract: Objective To investigate language outcomes in preschool children with hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) treated with therapeutic hypothermia and without major neurodevelopmental disabilities, and to identify early developmental and neonatal factors associated with language disorder at preschool age (LD). Methods This prospective longitudinal cohort study included children with moderate-to-severe HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia at a tertiary neonatal center and followed through preschool age. Children with cerebral palsy, intellectual disability (IQ <70), autism spectrum disorder, major genetic disorders, severe global developmental impairment, or other neurological conditions precluding reliable formal language assessment were excluded. Early developmental functioning was evaluated using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales at 24 months. Language skills were assessed between 30 and 76 months of age using standardized age-appropriate Italian instruments, and LD was identified on the basis of standardized assessment combined with clinical evaluation. Neonatal variables included cord blood pH, base excess, cerebral function monitoring, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Results Seventy-five children completed language assessment. Nineteen children (25.3%) met criteria for LD. Difficulties were more frequent in expressive language domains, with naming deficits observed in 62.7% and articulation/repetition difficulties in 61.3% of participants. Children who subsequently developed LD had significantly lower Griffiths Hearing and Speech (Scale C) scores at 24 months compared with children without LD [median 75 [IQR 67–80] vs. 88 [81–95], p < 0.001]. In logistic regression, each 10-point decrease in Griffiths Scale C was associated with higher odds of later LD (unadjusted OR 3.85, 95% CI 1.84–8.06; p < 0.001; adjusted OR 3.78, 95% CI 1.78–8.02; p < 0.001). Severe neonatal acidosis was associated with poorer comprehension and articulation/repetition outcomes, whereas combined white and gray matter injury was associated mainly with poorer expressive language performance. Discussion Language difficulties are common among preschool survivors of neonatal HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia, even in the absence of major neurological disabilities. Early language vulnerabilities are detectable at 24 months and may help identify children at increased risk of later LD, supporting the need for structured language surveillance within long-term follow-up programs.

title: Development and validation of a voice-based conversational artificial intelligence coaching agent to reduce competitive state anxiety in elite athletes: study protocol for a randomized, analyst-blinded, attention-matched active-controlled trial
abstract: Background Competitive state anxiety harms elite athletes’ performance and mental health, while stigma and training demands limit access to face-to-face support; voice-based conversational artificial intelligence (AI) analyzing speech in real time offers a scalable route to psychological skills training (PST). Methods Phase I develops the agent and tests content validity and usability against prespecified thresholds. Phase II is a parallel-group, analyst-blinded, attention-matched active-controlled randomized trial, fully online. All outcomes are self-reported by unblinded participants, so no outcome assessor is blinded; blinding covers the data manager and statistician. Eighty-six elite athletes registered with the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee are randomized 1:1 to 4 weeks of voice-based AI coaching (three sessions/week, ≥20 min) or a wordless relaxation recording, with delayed access. The arms match on dose, frequency and digital delivery but not on interactivity, content variety, platform or expectancy, so the trial estimates the incremental effect of the complete agent over a non-interactive comparator rather than isolating voice adaptation; credibility, expectancy, and adherence are measured and modeled in both arms. The primary endpoint is change from baseline to week 4 in Competitive State Anxiety Inventory-2 cognitive anxiety, administered within 24 h before the index competition nominated for each window; somatic anxiety and self-confidence follow in a fixed sequence. Secondary outcomes are GAD-7, PHQ-9, PSS-10, WHO-5 and SF-12; SUS and an AI voice-based anxiety index are exploratory. Timepoints are fixed relative to the first intervention session: baseline (before randomization), within 7 days after the intervention ends, and 2 weeks later; prespecified contingencies govern a canceled or postponed competition. Analysis is by linear mixed models (intention-to-treat). Discussion This may be among the first randomized trials of a conversational AI agent analyzing athletes’ speech in real time to deliver tailored PST. Strengths are phase I development, a dose-matched active comparator and a decentralized design, although the comparator does not isolate voice adaptation. Powered for d = 0.60 on the primary contrast, it is as much estimation as hypothesis testing. Clinical Trial Registration https://cris.nih.go.kr , identifier KCT0012076.

title: Early functional neuroimaging alterations in pTau217 biomarker-positive older adults
abstract: Introduction Early identification of individuals with Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is key to its successful management. In this regard, plasma biomarkers and functional magnetic resonance imaging alterations could represent useful triage tools for preclinical AD cases. Methods In this study, we analyzed the relationship between neuroimaging, biological and cognitive data from 88 elderly participants recruited from the University Hospital of Padua. Neuroimaging alterations were quantified based on a measure of dispersion within the connectivity gradient. LASSO and multiple linear regression models were used to specifically assess the interaction between gradients’ dispersion and plasma pTau217 levels in predicting cognitive performance, while controlling for cognitive reserve and renal dysfunction. Finally, exploratory ANCOVA models were used to test differences in dispersion between cognitively unimpaired individuals (UC), individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) who were pTau217-negative, individuals with prodromal AD (PR), defined by MCI status and pTau217 positivity, and a group of patients with more advanced AD from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Results Our results show that functional dispersion positively impacts cognitive performance in healthy participants, but only in crossmodal integration hubs and in tasks requiring multimodal processing. In PR individuals, however, dispersion within a wider profile of regions appeared to favor memory performance. Finally, dispersion values within several cortical regions were observed to significantly differ between UC and MCI individuals compared to AD, but not between PR and AD participants. Conclusion Although preliminary, our data delineate patterns of functional alterations in individuals with prodromal AD.

title: The digital mannequin: micro-trend mimesis and parasocial identity construction in emerging adult females on Instagram reels
abstract: This study examines the impact of Instagram Reels on the identity development of young female adults aged 18–25 years through an analysis of the interface between parasocial relations, micro-trend mimesis, and digital validation loops. Using semi-structured in-depth interviews, the study explores the effects of parasocial influence from individuals considered trendsetters on how a woman’s self-perception is shaped through continual viewing of short videos on Instagram. Additionally, it investigates how the imitation of micro-trends by women leads to the development of digital mannequins, which are aesthetically pleasing images that individuals express themselves as on social media platforms. The findings reveal that women are becoming increasingly reliant upon external sources of validation such as likes, comments, and shares to establish their self-worth and develop their identities. Grounded in Parasocial Relationship Theory, Social Comparison Theory, and Self-Discrepancy Theory, this research provides a better understanding of the pressures placed on emerging female adults by algorithm-driven social media environments toward making homogeneous and performative digital identities.

title: Real-Time AI-Based Smart Hearing Protection Prototype for Enhancing Safety Signal Audibility in Work Zones
venue: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
abstract: Abstract Hearing protection devices are essential for protecting the health of construction workers in job sites with loud noise; however, they may hinder workers’ ability to detect safety-critical alarms. Although previous research has demonstrated the potential of generative artificial intelligence (AI) models to enhance safety-critical sounds in construction work zones, the feasibility of real-time implementation of such models on wearable AI devices remains unclear. This study addresses that gap by developing and testing a novel AI-augmented hearing protector (AI-AHP) that deploys a real-time safety sound enhancement model on a low-cost Raspberry Pi 5 platform. The model was trained using various machine learning approaches on a data set comprising 4 types of safety-critical warning signals and 38 types of background noise. Controlled functionality testing, field deployment at active construction sites, and a subjective listener survey were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the prototype. The study identified DeepFilterNet as the most efficient model for edge computing, achieving fast and substantial improvements in signal audibility, with a maximum Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) improvement of 179%. Real-time operation was confirmed with a real-time factor of less than 1 and an end-to-end latency of 0.69 s on the Raspberry Pi 5. Subjective evaluation results showed significant increases in listener ratings, indicating that the enhanced signals were consistently perceived as clearer and more intelligible. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of deploying AI-driven hearing protection devices that improve worker situational awareness, reduce accident risk, and maintain usability in noisy construction environments, with potential applicability to other industrial settings.

title: GEPC: Generative-Explanatory Pest Classification with Multi-Modal Priors and Hierarchical Concept Constraints
abstract: Abstract Accurate and interpretable pest classification underpins precision agriculture and food security, yet three obstacles remain. Field-collected datasets are severely long-tailed, so rare and often high-risk pests are under-represented; closely related species are morphologically near-identical, limiting single-modality discrimination; and standard end-to-end classifiers emit labels without auditable reasoning. We present GEPC (Generative-Explanatory Pest Classifier), a unified framework organized around one principle: every prediction should be backed by a verifiable taxonomic pathway. To counter the long tail, a semantics-guided diffusion pipeline synthesizes ecologically plausible samples for rare classes through structured prompts and CLIP-based quality filtering, grounding augmentation in real taxonomic and habitat priors. For interpretability and fine-grained discrimination, GEPC casts feature extraction as non-negative, path-constrained sparse pursuit via Hierarchical Beam Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (HB-OMP) over an offline differential dictionary built on the Order--Family--Species tree, so the recovered root-to-leaf path denoises a frozen DINOv2 visual representation while doubling as a transparent diagnostic cue. This hierarchy-aligned signal is fused with species-anonymized morphological descriptions encoded by a frozen CLIP text encoder, and a lightweight classifier issues the final prediction. Across multiple random seeds on AP162, GEPC attains $90.4 \pm 0.3\%$ overall accuracy, $82.4\%$ tail-class recall, and $94.6\%$ agreement between the visual pursuit path and the final decision, consistently outperforming end-to-end supervised and zero-shot baselines while exposing the taxonomic evidence behind each prediction.

title: Real-world use of transcutaneous spinal neuromodulation combined with activity-based rehabilitation across neurological disorders: a retrospective post-market study
abstract: Background Transcutaneous spinal neuromodulation (TSN) is the first therapy approved by US FDA and is delivered in conjunction with activity-based rehabilitation, but evidence describing routine clinical use across heterogeneous neurological populations remains limited. Objective To characterize the real-world implementation and documented safety of TSN delivered via xStep-assisted rehabilitation and to describe within-participant changes in routinely collected clinical outcomes. Methods This retrospective observational study reviewed de-identified records from 50 individuals with cerebral palsy (CP; n = 29), spinal cord injury (SCI; n = 11), or other neurological or structural conditions ( n = 10). xStep was incorporated into individualized activity-based rehabilitation for approximately 1 h per session, 2–5 days per week. Outcomes available in routine records included hand-held dynamometry, Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), International Standards for Neurological Classification of Spinal Cord Injury motor and sensory scores, 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), and Timed Up and Go (TUG) test. Analyses were descriptive; outcome-specific denominators are reported. Results During same-session dynamometry, mean force increased from 5.41 N without stimulation to 6.00 N with stimulation across 12 participants; 10 of 12 had a net increase in mean force. Spasticity decreased in at least one assessed muscle group in 13 of 24 participants. Among eight participants with SCI and paired assessments, mean motor score changed from 44.12 to 45.50 and mean sensory score from 124.62 to 129.12. Descriptive improvements were also observed in gait speed and TUG completion time among ambulatory participants, with variable assessment intervals and no untreated comparator. No device-related adverse event, serious adverse event, neurological deterioration, or device-related treatment discontinuation was documented in the reviewed records. Conclusions xStep was integrated into individualized neurorehabilitation without documented device-related adverse events or treatment discontinuations in this retrospective cohort. The observed within-participant changes are clinical signals and do not establish efficacy or causality. Diagnosis-specific prospective studies with standardized exposure, predefined endpoints, and comparator conditions are needed.

title: Adversarial example detection for image captioning models via SPC-verify
abstract: Image captioning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples that can induce descriptions inconsistent with visual evidence, commonsense knowledge, or physical rules. Existing detection methods mainly rely on confidence anomalies, feature-space deviations, or reconstruction errors, making them less suitable for cross-modal generative tasks. To address this limitation, we propose SPC-Verify, a Semantic-Phenomenon Consistency Verification framework for adversarial example detection in image captioning. The framework combines Visual-Semantic Consistency Verification (VSCV), which assesses whether token-level visual evidence supports the corresponding generated concepts, with Phenomenon Plausibility Verification (PPV), which evaluates the consistency of complete captions with commonsense knowledge and physical constraints. To improve the reliability of local visual evidence, we introduce SCAR-SAT, a post-hoc heatmap refinement method for Show-Attend-and-Tell-based models that integrates semantic consistency, lightweight counterfactual support, spatial continuity, and temporal stability. We further propose Zero-Shot Cross-Model Threshold Transfer (ZS-CMTT), which learns shared decision thresholds from the joint score distributions of SAT and BLIP and transfers them to unseen captioning models without requiring target-model samples. Experiments on MSCOCO and Flickr30K across SAT and BLIP, under multiple attack settings, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Ablation studies show that the Grounded Category Vocabulary improves token-level verification, while PPV provides complementary sentence-level plausibility assessment. Further evaluations indicate that SCAR-SAT improves token-level visual grounding and that ZS-CMTT facilitates threshold transfer across captioning models. Overall, SPC-Verify provides an interpretable and transferable approach to adversarial example detection by jointly evaluating local visual-semantic consistency and global caption plausibility.

title: Companionship-oriented conversational AI use and loneliness among community-dwelling older adults: the moderating role of human social connectedness
abstract: Background Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for companionship, creating new questions about loneliness and social relationships in later life. We examined the association between AI companionship use and loneliness, its variation across levels of human social connectedness, and emotional dependence among users. Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey conducted in Guangzhou between March and May 2026 included a nonprobability, complete-case sample of 427 community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older. Loneliness was measured using the three-item UCLA scale and human connectedness using the six-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6). Linear regressions used HC3 covariance estimates and adjusted for demographic, household, health and digital circumstances. An interaction model assessed variation across connectedness levels, and a separate analysis examined study-specific emotional dependence among 168 AI companionship users. Results Of the 427 respondents, 168 (39.3%) used AI for companionship. At mean connectedness, the adjusted loneliness difference between users and nonusers was −1.175 points (95% CI − 1.459 to −0.891). The AI-by-connectedness coefficient was 0.587 per five LSNS-6 points (95% CI 0.346 to 0.827). Adjusted differences were −1.610, −1.140 and −0.671 points at the lower quartile, median and upper quartile of connectedness, respectively. Among users, each dependence point was associated with 0.752 additional loneliness points (95% CI 0.493 to 1.010), adjusting for frequency, connectedness and contextual covariates. Conclusion AI companionship use was associated with lower loneliness, particularly among respondents with weaker human connectedness. Greater emotional dependence was associated with higher loneliness among users. These concurrent associations support assessing digital companionship alongside human network resources and emotional reliance, while prospective studies are needed to establish temporal relationships and evaluate intervention benefits or harms.

title: Note2Narr: a neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for synthesizing high-fidelity training narratives from sparse counselor notes
abstract: Introduction Early identification of mental health risks among university students requires high-quality, privacy-conscious dialogue data for developing and evaluating computational screening models. Existing synthetic datasets often lack the contextual nuance and diagnostic consistency needed to preserve clinically relevant psychological signals. Methods We introduce Note2Narr, a neuro-symbolic framework for synthesizing high-fidelity training narratives from sparse counselor notes. A Dynamic Counseling Tree guides inquiry from broad topic exploration to in-depth probing of personal experiences. A Supervisor Agent equipped with a Chain of Psychological Clues audits the safety and consistency of generated narratives, while a Fictional Detail Generator incorporates diverse, disorder-neutral personal experiences. A Vendi Score-guided 1-to-X strategy adaptively allocates the number of narrative variants. Evaluation combines blinded human assessment, LLM-based assessment, student-disjoint downstream prediction, and a label-leakage audit with masking ablation. Results The framework produced 981 multi-turn counseling dialogues comprising 11,145 question-answer turns from 224 source students. Blinded human comparisons with MDD-5K identified statistically significant improvements in Professionalism, Communication, Participation, Repetition, and Authenticity after Holm correction. Downstream text classifiers achieved macro-AUROC and macro-AUPRC values of up to 0.739 and 0.405, respectively. Masking explicit diagnostic cues changed macro-AUPRC by at most 0.005, suggesting that predictive utility was not driven solely by direct diagnostic wording. Discussion These findings support Note2Narr as a framework for constructing synthetic counseling corpora for privacy-conscious dialogue modeling and screening-oriented research. The results demonstrate learnable associations in synthetic narratives; prospective and external validation remains necessary before applied use.

title: TEMPO-taVNS: a multimodal platform optimizing thermal, electrical, and mechanical auricular stimulation
abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is typically delivered electrically, while alternative stimulation modalities and their potential for personalization remain underexplored. We present TEMPO-taVNS (Thermal, Electrical, and Mechanical Parameter Optimization for taVNS), a human-centered methodology for multimodal auricular neuromodulation designed to explore and optimize stimulation of sensory pathways associated with the auricular branch of the vagus nerve (ABVN). The platform integrates custom hardware capable of delivering thermal, vibrotactile, and electrical stimulation with software that enables systematic parameter sweeps. Responses are characterized through high-resolution physiological monitoring including heart rate, heart rate variability, gastric slow-wave activity, pupil diameter, beat-to-beat blood pressure, brain response activity, and electrodermal activity, together with participant-reported perception and comfort. To address interindividual variability, a Pareto-front Gaussian-process optimization framework identifies personalized stimulation parameters by balancing physiological response with user comfort. We further describe experimental protocols for evaluating this multimodal parameter space in humans. Together, the hardware, software, physiological sensing, and optimization framework provide a scalable foundation for individualized, non-invasive and nonpharmacological auricular neuromodulation, and for investigating non-electrical approaches to vagal stimulation for wearable neuromodulation systems.
